R-A.description: Editor rows from several series. The early IR authoring rows (R-A, R-B, R-B10, R-B12, R-C, R-D, R-F, R-G, R-H) keep every tab mounted with the inactive ones hidden, show errors in one panel-level strip, write both edge endpoints or neither with the endpoint logic in a pure module, ratify the climb to the parent per feature in endpoints, keep persisted waypoints when routing is not orthogonal and register no path for those edges, leave the metaclass pin out of `canonicalize`, and move the legacy Name and parent controls into the Applies to tab; R-IRN-3 flags a degraded custom view in authoring instead of on the canvas, and R-GV-16 and 17 make the toolbar Auto layout keep graphVertex containment and a framing container follow a dragged child, with a size set by hand as its floor. JjScript makes a `create` all-or-nothing on its superclasses (R-JS-1), and Run (R-JS-2 to 7) lets the dependency wait accept a bare name only when the bound metamodel resolves it, runs in passes that defer and retry forward references, a retry pass waiting for every dependency, never pauses on an error and closes with one summary modal; undo in editor-v2 (R-UNDO-1 to 7) keeps the D-layer undo as the only one, gated by `U.userHasInteracted`, advances the project version only on an explicit save, makes a rename one dispatch, and measures that «create a view and open it» is one step while a selection alone is none, and R-LAY-19 (several canvases of one model, each under its own viewpoint, the layout key taken from the canvas and no new reader of `state.viewpoint` in editor-v2) is what R-UNDO-4 waits on to take viewpoint activation out of undo. 15 of 27 rows are realized: all of R-JS, R-LAY-19, R-GV-17, R-A, R-B, R-B10, R-B12, R-D and R-H; R-C, R-F, R-G, R-GV-16, R-IRN-3 and R-UNDO-1 to 7 are not.

R-B9.description: Derived viewpoints and how they are drawn. The «Derive viewpoint» dialog picks a notation (Generic by default, Petri net and its classic variant, Statechart (UML), Flowchart (ISO 5807), Activity (UML), ER (Chen) among them) and a metaclass to role table; the notations bring optional IR keys and persisted values (five text and label keys, the entry mark, the arc, the end labels, the `hollowCircle` termination) under R-B9's rule that a persisted name such as a routing value never changes, every derived arrowhead is open, Activity (UML) gains view-only decision and merge diamonds, a styled guard and a fork and join bar, the default notation is made legible in the light theme, and the run's token is drawn as a dot inside a derived node. Three other threads: «Color by metaclass» on the viewpoint panel (twelve pastel swatches assigned along references, per-metaclass overrides, notation glyphs left uncoloured), the toolbar auto-layout with ELK in full (per-notation profiles, routes drawn and never persisted, outside labels reserved in its input), and seven more edge ends with conditional ends and end labels (R-EE-1 to 4); two rows from other series sit here, the model-wide M1 name lookup of JjScript (R-JS-10) and the copy-on-write fix of `CompositeActionReducer` that makes every slot write undoable (R-UNDO-8). 31 of 49 rows are realized, R-JS-10 among them; not realized are the ELK rows R-VP-40 to 48, the edge ends R-EE-1 to 4, R-VP-52, 58 and 59, R-VP-60 (withdrawn), and R-UNDO-8.

R-B9-bis.description: Three threads that meet in the IR read context and in `validateIR`, whose rules belong to authoring and never to render (R-B9-bis): IR edges (the `container` endpoint and its reactivity, object-as-edge synthesis and deletion), JjEL as the IR expression language (R-J1 to 7: a closed profile, legacy multi-hop paths migrated, `getParent` on `ReadCtx`, diagnostics always on), and the `marked` predicate (R-MK-1 to 11), read from the ephemeral run state through `ReadCtx.isMarked` and invalidated through declared dependency channels. R-IRN-4 adds the IR seed written when a view is created. Realized: R-B9-bis, R-B13 to 16 and all of R-MK; R-B17 (deleting an object-as-edge), R-IRN-4 and all of R-J are not.

R-DEAD-1.description: Retiring the seeded default views, and layout per viewpoint. The R-IRN rows (1, 2, 7 to 24, 27) make `ir` mean authored notation, declare the classic canvas v1 unreachable, stop seeding `Default Validation`, hide `Default` as a system layer while it holds no authored view, make the empty viewpoint `null` on both sides of the proxy, retire the seed in VersionFixer pass `2.228` with the purge of saved defaults split off, and find the `updateDefaultView` refresh button unreachable; the R-LAY rows (1 to 18) keep a `layoutByViewpoint` record per exclusive viewpoint on `DVertex`, abstract syntax included under its own `__abstract__` key, read through to the seed scalars, behind one resolver and one source of the active viewpoint. The rest is the removal of the dead `NestedView` and its cascade (R-DEAD-1 to 6), channel edges hidden by `containment.edges: 'hide'`, absent meaning show (R-GV-4), and two method rules: extend an existing discovery report with an addendum (R-E/E-1) and prove the search behind an assertion of absence or presence (R-RAIL-28). 19 of 48 rows are realized: R-LAY-9 to 11 and 14 to 18, the seed and empty-viewpoint steps R-IRN-8 to 10, 15, 18 to 20 and 23, R-DEAD-5, R-GV-4 and R-E/E-1; the other R-IRN rows, the layout principles R-LAY-1 to 8 and the findings R-LAY-12 and 13, the dead-code rows except R-DEAD-5, and R-RAIL-28 are not.

R-DMV-1.description: The Data Manager and the form engine behind it, with the placement rules they replaced or refined. The Data Manager Viewpoint (R-DMV-1 to 7) is one built-in viewpoint per project whose class views without `shape` give the table columns and the drawer form, materialized at the first write; it supersedes R-VP-3 and R-VP-12 of the earlier rows R-VP-1 to 13, which place validity in the metamodel and presentation in the viewpoint, freeze the `jjodel/*` keys, set a three-rung renderer ladder (viewpoint, type, default) and limit the manager form to fields, order, sections, renderer and label. The form engine rows (R-FORM, R-WCX, R-STR) make the manager a sibling surface of the canvas over a pure engine in `jjform/` with D-graph and JSON adapters, keep the renderer precedence in the engine, record what an adapter must do (the containment cascade, deferred deletes after a write, `setName` as a primitive of its own) and let the view win in the form and, since R-STR-6 was closed, on the canvas too. 20 of 40 rows are realized; ten of the fifteen R-FORM rows, the placement criteria R-VP-1, 2 and 4 to 7, R-WCX-2 and 3, R-DMV-2 and R-DMV-7 are not.

R-EDGE-1.description: The core of the simulation engine and its configuration, with three rows on metamodel canvas edges. Simulator rows: the Petri transition as the core, with fork, join and `else` compiled onto it, bounded weighted markings, termination distinct from deadlock and five run states; system profiles over one role catalogue, computed required roles, `simProfile` and a pure binder behind Apply; declared state attributes (stored, derived with eager evaluation and cycle checks, input variables chosen by the environment) persisted in the additive `simStateAttributes` key and decoded record by record, entry, exit and arc actions, with the guards and actions of a triggered transition reading the firing event as `event.a`, accepting places, Moore and Mealy outputs, the activity final role, compile defects listed at Reset, and panel lines that give the reason a guard blocks without moving the buttons. R-EDGE-1 to 3 accept a metamodel connection only between class nodes, guard the model invariant in the core setters and the Ecore import linker in a separate lane, and defer any migration of saved projects. 53 of 57 rows are realized; R-EDGE-3, R-SIM-83 (the engine reads the activity final), 84 (`else` on fused transitions and the `else-position` defect) and 85 (the `sim-modal` branch on the trunk before the 2026-10-01 freeze) are not.

R-GEN-1.description: Three threads: the code generation pilot (R-GEN-1 to 17), to ship in 3.2 (live by 2026-10-26, content freeze 2026-10-23) behind an experimental setting off by default, with templates as JjEL functions with string interpolation stored as `genTemplates` in the metamodel's `_state`, every copied fragment recording its origin, JavaScript as the one target in an isolated Web Worker, and an oracle that compares it with the simulator step by step, in 3.2 only if green by the freeze; the simulator's run tools (R-SIM-134 to 143 and 146): clocks that may start with the run and belong to it, watches as invariants and breakpoints, step back, scenarios, coverage, a timeline slider and the board editor layout; and parity between the IR object view and the native renderer (R-IRN-29 to 36), chrome rather than geometry, with `underline`, label `color` and `cornerRadius` added to the IR without migration, the separator taking the border colour, and migrated views identified by a `migratedHash` stamp since 2026-09-24. Smaller rows: Entry, Exit, Action and Guard made multi-valued (R-SIM-90), a feature on a sibling owner judged a warning in the role checks when a common concrete subclass exists (R-SIM-89), metaclass identity across metamodels through `authoringMetaclassPins` (R-MCID-1, 2), flat collapse fields of a graphVertex (R-IRN-37), the renderer inspector mounted on the IR branch so rung 0 of the renderer precedence is reachable on the canvas (R-STR-7), and R-RAIL-31, on quoting shell globs in prompts, a stray. 33 of 43 rows are realized; R-GEN-1 (the 3.2 date), 8 and 9 (the oracle as a goal, what stays out of the pilot), 13 (the legacy M2T left as it is), R-IRN-32, 34, 36 and 37, R-MCID-2 and R-RAIL-31 are not.

R-IRN-38.description: Editing IR labels and row values in place on the canvas, and the panel toggles that show it. One predicate decides whether a name label renames the element (R-IRN-38), a path label on an attribute of its own object edits only when the IR opts in (R-IRN-41), the value-segment toggle reads the effective `editable` value (R-IRN-40), and node and row subscriptions carry the object and metaclass names so labels follow a rename (R-IRN-39). All four rows are provisional; R-IRN-38 and R-IRN-41 are realized, R-IRN-39 and R-IRN-40 are not.

R-M2U-1.description: Name uniqueness in the metamodel (M2). Names are case-sensitive and a near-homonym such as `Foo` beside `foo` is announced with a warning, not refused; classes and enumerations share one namespace across the whole metamodel, datatypes get a namespace of their own, and inherited features enter the class namespace, so shadowing is refused. The duplicate-name badge now covers M2 and the JjScript rename goes through the name setter. R-M2U-1, 2, 4 and 6 are realized; R-M2U-3 (the datatype namespace) and R-M2U-5 (the dead step 2 of `get_type`, kept and declared) are not.

R-RAIL-1.description: The properties rail and the rules learned while building it. Design rows: the rail is a shell with an inspector slot and only preset `2a`, the tree pane reuses `TreeViewContent` with a restyle, the NODE section stays in the shell behind `advanced` and closed by default, the identity block restyle moves to arc 2, the shell breadcrumb drops the metamodel segment, the shell shows abstractness as italics on the name, and tokens are consumed under fixed rules (a blacklist of 13 conflicting names, snapping to the scale, an OKLCH entity scale with one source, kept out of the tree). Method rows written along the way: conformance greps on the staged diff, the interactive `grep` as a `ugrep` wrapper, a computed style measured only on the element that paints, an order read from the data and not from a position; R-RAIL-44, the dark theme suspended, is now superseded by D-UI-15. 10 of 33 rows are realized (R-RAIL-7, 10, 14, 30, 32, 33, 34, 36, 42 and 45); the rest are not.

R-SGL-1.description: Singleton classes in M1. The singleton instance exists by construction and no path creates one (palette, canvas drop, composition menu, JjScript), switching the flag off removes every instance, the switch-on guard counts instances per model, and the «singleton» stereotype shows only on the abstract syntax. With singletons hidden, a reference to a singleton-conforming type is assigned from a select (commit B, IR branch only). R-SGL-1 to 4 and R-SGL-8 are realized; the commit plan (R-SGL-5), the six instantiation filters (R-SGL-6), the issues recorded but not closed (R-SGL-9) and the perimeter of commit B (R-SGL-10) are not.

R-SIM-1.description: Foundations of the simulation engine. The run state lives outside Redux, one per model, and the configuration sits as flat `sim*` keys in the bag of the M2 model, with `set_state`, history and the collaborative channel unchanged for v1; a step interleaves with a selector instead of firing everything, its actions form one parallel assignment over the previous state, an absent guard is true and a malformed one takes the arc out of the candidates, and events are M1 instances with one panel button each, configured from the Trigger reference. A dozen rows build the guard and action language, kept within a subset exportable to nuXmv: the `Expression` and `Action` primitive types in the core with their migration and Ecore form, the `.[x]` operator over semantic state and `node.[x]` over presentation state, strict parsing, reserved names, the evaluator hook, the marking accessor and inhibitor arcs read as guards through it; R-SIM-19 declares state attributes per metaclass as in an attribute grammar, stored (written by actions) or derived (a JjEL equation with a circularity check). 23 of 30 rows are realized; R-SIM-9 (initial rule per STC genre), 10 (`simSource`), 11 (`marked` as a derived view), 12 (events as M1 instances), 14 (a pure core in `model/simulation/`), 19 (the attribute declarations) and 20 (no stability before an event) are not.

R-SIM-3.description: What the user sees and touches during a simulation run, which never writes the model. The run panel rows: the panel outside the IR, the run withdrawn when the model changes, the Simulation pill shown in Advanced mode on a metamodel whose Simulation toggle is on, a compact panel that shows state (watched attributes, marking, events) above a transport row that does not move, nondeterministic choices resolved by Ask or Random with Play, σ and `node` shown apart with nuXmv names, a two-column State page in the roles dialog, a navigable trace, `node.[x]` readable by viewpoints, and a transition blocked by its guard read as `guard false`; with them a role set `off` read as unbound, Accepting read by the engine, the DFA, NFA, Moore and Mealy presets shown before the freeze, and globals declared in the model. The I/O board (R-SIM-110 to 133) is the machine's environment, not a view: a device library (buttons, switches, sliders, keypad, clock, LEDs, displays, buzzer) bound to events, inputs and expressions over σ, saved with the model, with an editor, two skins, themes, spans, icons suggested from event names, keycaps and a floating window; pins, skin, window place and sound are viewer preferences, kept out of the model. 41 of 48 rows are realized; R-SIM-92 (role outputs in the engine), 93 (the accepting and output keys made definitive), 105 (the run inspector), 107 (the opt-in σ overlay), 116 and 117 (the `ioBoard` key and the binding forms) and 129 (what stays out of the first cut) are not.

R-SKIN-1.description: Form appearance presets: a closed catalogue (Slate, Paper, Ink, Mist; Slate is today's look and the default) that remaps the existing form tokens in `styles/tokens/`, orthogonal to the layout theme and with nothing the user can customise. R-SKIN-3-bis renames the vocabulary to palette (`formPalette`, `data-palette`) and moves the attribute to the `.instance-manager` root, the name persisted on the Data Manager Viewpoint singleton; R-SKIN-4 leaves the per-view skins of `irTypes.ts` untouched. All five rows are ratified and none is realized.

R-VAL-1.description: User-defined validation as a concern with its own viewpoints, separate from the syntax viewpoints, multiple and selectable, with rules activated per viewpoint and per rule. In the first slice a rule is owned by an M2 class; it is a type parallel to the view (not a `DViewElement`), accumulates with superclass rules instead of overriding them, and never blocks a write; a broken rule shows in authoring and a false one in the problems registry. Further rows cover a single reserved-name list, deleting a class that has rules, rules travelling with an imported metamodel, and no rule sign in the rail. Realized: R-VAL-1, 5, 6-bis, 7, 11 and 12; R-VAL-2, 3, 4, 6, 8, 9 and 10 are not.
